title: InfrastructureContract v0.1
$comment: closed at the root (D1170): the runtime refuses a top-level key it does not read, and until this was written the published schema did not — a `constraint:` (singular) block, the exact defect D673 refused, validated here without a word. `x-` is the escape, on both sides.

^x-.$comment: the escape a document uses for data the runtime deliberately does not read

items.$comment: closed (D1161): a contract is where a REQUIREMENT is declared, so a key nothing reads is a requirement that never existed while the document validates. `x-` is the escape the top level has published since D673 and it travels with the rule.

type.description: The capability types v0.1 recognises. Held equal to the runtime's set and the reference implementation's (D1150) — a third party validating against this file must not be refused a type the tool accepts.

state.description: D47: retirement is explicit, never absence

requirements.$comment: D8's short form for a hard constraint, and it is STATIC-bar sugar: the loader builds the constraint with `verify: {method: static}` and reads nothing else here. A `verify:` written in a requirement used to be dropped in silence, so the same residency rule blocked as a constraint and passed as sugar (D1166). Closed, so writing one is a refusal that names where the bar belongs.

items.$comment: an assumption is a RECORD: it travels in the contract's hash, into an audit and into a capsule, and `affects` is reference-checked. It does not change a verdict — the summary's verdictsOnAssumedValues comes from the CANDIDATE's provenance — so this block is documentary, which is different from reserved: it does exactly what its name promises. Closed anyway, because a misspelled `confidance` drops the number from the record and a reader cannot tell that from nobody having stated one.

autonomy.$comment: the consent block. It published NOTHING about its shape while the runtime read eight keys, so a reader had no way to learn the vocabulary except from an example — and a misspelling silently disarmed a gate (D1164). Closed, with the `x-` escape the rest of the document carries.

auto_execute.$comment: reserved in v0 (D1164): shape-gated as a mapping and read by NOTHING. `max_reversibility` and `max_cost_delta` appear nowhere in either implementation, so a contract capping what may execute automatically caps nothing. It is in the flagship example, which is why it is labelled rather than left to be discovered. Held by TestAReservedBlockChangesNothingButTheHash.

outcomes.$comment: reserved in v0 (D1163): NOTHING in the runtime reads this block. It is parsed, shape-gated and folded into the contract's hash, and no verb changes behaviour because of it — `probe` derives what to measure from the ledger's bindings and reads the contract only for the intrusive-probe consent (D59). Declared here rather than left to be inferred, because it appears in a shipped example and a reader who writes it is entitled to know it does nothing yet. Held by TestAReservedBlockChangesNothingButTheHash: adding the block may change the contract's hash and nothing else, so implementing it fails that gate until this marker comes off.

verify.$comment: closed (D1162), and it publishes BOTH spellings of a bar. It listed only `method` while the loader has read `design`+`runtime` since D728, so a contract using the two-bar form was valid for the runtime and invalid against this document. Closed because the block is guarded against every wrong VALUE and was blind to a wrong KEY: `method` defaults to `static`, so `vrify:` or `methdo:` silently traded provider evidence for the candidate's own word.

budgetConstraint.$comment: a constraint that carries its own severity — the loader reads `severity` from a budget entry and defaults it to `hard`, and this file used to point budget at $defs/constraint, which never published the field (D1162). Its own definition rather than a key added to `constraint`, so a HARD constraint cannot carry a severity the runtime would ignore.
